title: rowToArtifact throws on one corrupt row and fails the whole catalog read
body:
## Summary
listArtifacts/listAllArtifacts/listDeferredArtifacts/getArtifact JSON.parse each row's data and ue_assets unguarded, so one unparseable blob 500s every full-row read of its catalog (and the global drain queue).

## Description
src/lib/pipeline-artifacts-db.ts:249-261 `rowToArtifact` does `JSON.parse(row.data)` / `JSON.parse(row.ue_assets)` with no guard. The same module already anticipates a non-JSON blob: `hashOfBlob` (src/lib/pipeline-artifacts-db.ts:173) and `listArtifactVerdicts` (src/lib/pipeline-artifacts-db.ts:279) degrade to 'no binding' for it, and the sibling store documents a degrade-don't-throw contract (`parseUeAssets` src/lib/catalog-db.ts:36, `rowToEntity` src/lib/catalog-db.ts:175). Two implementations of one rule, one fixed. Fixed looks like: a per-row degrade that keeps the row VISIBLE as corrupt (status/reason marking `CORRUPT: data unparseable`) and logs it - never a silent `{}` that a later re-upsert could write back over the real blob. That choice (what a degraded row looks like to graders and writers) is why this is not Lane A.

## Flow
- a bypass writer (older checkout on the shared DB, manual SQL) leaves one row's data unparseable
- GET /api/pipeline-artifacts?catalogId=X -> listArtifacts -> rowToArtifact throws -> 500 for the whole catalog
- the drain queue (listDeferredArtifacts) and settle/package (listAllArtifacts) fail the same way
- fix: guarded parse in rowToArtifact returning a marked degraded row + logger.error; writers refuse to persist the placeholder

## Expected impact
Operators stop losing a whole catalog's lab view / drain queue to one bad row; measured by the probe going from THROW to rows=N with the bad row marked. Could break: a grader that treats the degraded row as real content if the marker is not honoured.

## Evaluation
Claim: resilience - one corrupt row no longer fails every full-row read of its catalog
Before: probe on a throwaway DB (2 rows, 1 corrupted): listArtifacts -> THROW `Expected property name or '}' in JSON at position 1`; listArtifactVerdicts -> rows=2
After: predicted: listArtifacts -> rows=2 with the corrupt row marked; not built because the degraded-row shape is a semantic decision
Method: probe - corrupted one row in a POF_DB_PATH DB and called both readers; the After needs the degraded-row shape chosen first
Result: better
Gate: contract
evidence:
src/lib/pipeline-artifacts-db.ts:254 data: JSON.parse((row.data as string) || '{}'),
src/lib/pipeline-artifacts-db.ts:255 ueAssets: JSON.parse((row.ue_assets as string) || '[]'),
src/lib/catalog-db.ts:36 parseUeAssets (degrade-don't-throw)
probe: listArtifacts: THROW ...; listArtifactVerdicts: rows=2
14 import sites of the four full-row readers outside the module
instrument: vitest on POF_DB_PATH: corrupt one of two rows, assert listArtifacts/listAllArtifacts/listDeferredArtifacts return both rows with the corrupt one marked, and upsertArtifact refuses to persist the placeholder

title: Bestiary ability links resolve 8 of 287 named abilities, silently
body:
## Summary
seed-bestiary resolves each archetype ability to a spellbook id by exact name and drops misses without a trace: 279 of 287 names resolve to nothing; characters drop 'Heavy Attack' (2 of 4 resolve).

## Description
src/lib/catalog/seed-bestiary.ts:20-30 `resolveLinks` looks each `archetype.abilities` name up in a case-insensitive spellbook name index and silently skips a miss; src/lib/catalog/seed-characters.ts:13-27 is a byte-identical second copy of the same index + rule. Enemy abilities ('Enemy Swing', 'Shadow Bolt', 'Force Lightning', ...) mostly have no spellbook entry, so the bestiary->spellbook 'ability' link graph is ~97% absent and nothing reports it. Fixed looks like: one shared resolver, an exported unresolved list, and a ratchet test pinning the resolved count so it only grows; closing the gap needs spellbook data or an alias map, which is a content decision.

## Flow
- seed-bestiary builds links for 94 archetypes
- 279 of 287 ability names have no spellbook name match -> no link, no log
- seed-characters: 'Heavy Attack' unresolved for both characters
- fix order: extract shared resolver -> expose unresolved -> ratchet test -> (operator) add spellbook entries or alias map

## Expected impact
Cross-catalog navigation and link checkers (acceptance/linkCheckers.ts reads data.links) see the real ability graph; measured as resolved link count. Could break: data additions shift seeds other tests snapshot.

## Evaluation
Claim: quality - ability links in the design data actually resolve
Before: probe over ARCHETYPES x seedSpellbookEntries(): total=287, unresolved=279 (resolved 8); characters 2 of 4 resolved
After: unmeasured - depends on which abilities get spellbook entries or aliases
Method: probe - counted resolutions with a throwaway vitest; the After needs content, not code
Result: unmeasurable
Gate: direction
evidence:
src/lib/catalog/seed-bestiary.ts:23 const id = SPELLBOOK_BY_NAME.get(abilityName.toLowerCase());
src/lib/catalog/seed-bestiary.ts:24 if (id) links.push(...)   // miss = silent drop
src/lib/catalog/seed-characters.ts:13-18 duplicate buildSpellbookNameIndex
probe: total=287 unresolved=279 [melee-grunt:Enemy Swing, ranged-caster:Shadow Bolt, brute:Charge Attack, ...]
instrument: ratchet test counting resolved bestiary+character ability links (8+2 today), failing on decrease; operator decides alias map vs new spellbook entries

title: pipelineStore track state has no reader; its only writer hook has no caller
body:
## Summary
usePipelineStore's tracksByEntity is written only by useEntityTrackHelp, which nothing calls, and useEntityTracks/setTrackState/getEntityTracks have no non-test consumer.

## Description
src/stores/pipelineStore.ts:30-57 exposes loadTracks/setTrackState/getEntityTracks/useEntityTracks. Grep over src excluding __tests__ and the store: `usePipelineStore` -> only src/hooks/useEntityTrackHelp.ts:9; `useEntityTrackHelp(` -> only its own definition (src/hooks/useEntityTrackHelp.ts:30); `useEntityTracks`, `setTrackState`, `getEntityTracks` -> 0. The client track cache is write-only and its single writer is unreachable. Its doc also says loadTracks 'Merge[s]' (src/stores/pipelineStore.ts:14) while it REPLACES the entity's map. Fixed: delete hook + store + store test, or wire a real consumer if the ECW track UI is still planned. The hook is outside this context's paths.

## Flow
- grep usePipelineStore -> 1 hit (useEntityTrackHelp)
- grep useEntityTrackHelp( -> 0 callers
- grep useEntityTracks|setTrackState|getEntityTracks outside store/tests -> 0
- fix: remove src/hooks/useEntityTrackHelp.ts, src/stores/pipelineStore.ts, src/__tests__/stores/pipelineStore.test.ts (or wire a consumer)

## Expected impact
Less dead client state; measured as files/exports removed (3 files, 6 exports). Could break: a planned ECW track UI that intended to use it.

## Evaluation
Claim: quality - remove a write-only store and its uncalled writer
Before: useEntityTrackHelp 0 callers; useEntityTracks/setTrackState/getEntityTracks 0 non-test consumers
After: predicted 3 files removed, typecheck + vitest green
Method: probe - zero-consumer greps run; deletion spans src/hooks (outside this context)
Result: better
Gate: none
evidence:
grep -rn usePipelineStore src (non-test) -> src/hooks/useEntityTrackHelp.ts:9,32
grep useEntityTrackHelp( -> src/hooks/useEntityTrackHelp.ts:30 only
src/stores/pipelineStore.ts:14 doc says Merge; :36-41 replaces
instrument: delete the 3 files in a worktree; typecheck + full vitest green; grep shows 0 dangling imports

title: WIRING-AND-ACCEPTANCE.md misstates who writes catalog_lifecycle and catalog_entities
body:
## Summary
docs/catalog/WIRING-AND-ACCEPTANCE.md:8-9 says catalog_lifecycle is gated by resolveTransition in POST /api/catalog and catalog_entities is written only through POST /api/catalog-entities; the code has one derived lifecycle writer and four entity writers.

## Description
docs/catalog/WIRING-AND-ACCEPTANCE.md:8: `Written by the @@CALLBACK system -> POST /api/catalog -> upsertLifecycle, gated by resolveTransition`. The route (src/app/api/catalog/route.ts) records ueAssets then defers to `syncEntityLifecycle`; docs/catalog/index.md:41 says the opposite ('walks no ladder ... ONE lifecycle writer: the derivation'). WIRING:9: catalog_entities 'Written through POST /api/catalog-entities only' - but upsertEntity is also called from src/lib/catalog/pipelines/contracts/contractsSync.ts:105 (source 'ingest') and src/lib/game-intake-db.ts:173, and src/lib/catalog-db.ts:134 inserts games/<id>/entities.json rows on first read. Fixed: rewrite both bullets to match index.md and name the four writers.

## Flow
- read WIRING:8-9
- grep upsertEntity( -> 3 call sites + the file-restore insert
- compare to docs/catalog/index.md:41
- fix: edit the two bullets (docs/ is director-owned this night)

## Expected impact
An agent reading the wiring doc no longer re-adds a resolveTransition ladder to the callback or assumes one entity writer. Could break: nothing.

## Evaluation
Claim: quality - doc statements match code
Before: 2 false statements in WIRING:8-9 (1 contradicts index.md:41); 4 real catalog_entities writers vs 1 documented
After: 0 false statements
Method: probe - each claim traced to code; doc edit not built because docs/ is director-owned
Result: better
Gate: none
evidence:
docs/catalog/WIRING-AND-ACCEPTANCE.md:8 ... gated by `resolveTransition`
docs/catalog/WIRING-AND-ACCEPTANCE.md:9 Written through `POST /api/catalog-entities` only
src/lib/catalog/pipelines/contracts/contractsSync.ts:105 upsertEntity(... source: 'ingest')
src/lib/game-intake-db.ts:173 upsertEntity(... source: 'user')
instrument: doc edit + grep that every upsertEntity caller is named in the doc

title: Settle POST reports a malformed body as 'catalogId is required'
body:
## Summary
POST /api/pipeline-artifacts/settle parses its body with req.json().catch(() => ({})), so malformed JSON is refused with a misleading missing-catalogId reason.

## Description
src/app/api/pipeline-artifacts/settle/route.ts:98. Not dangerous (a missing catalogId is already a 400, unlike the drain route fixed this round in f62f5e06), but the reason is wrong: an operator who sent a truncated `{"catalogId":"items"` is told the field is missing. Fixed: the drain route's empty-vs-invalid split - empty body {}, unparseable -> 400 'not valid JSON'.

## Flow
- POST settle with a truncated body -> 400 'catalogId is required' (misleading)
- fix: text() + JSON.parse with a distinct 400

## Expected impact
Truthful refusal reason (Rule 4c). Could break: nothing; status code unchanged.

## Evaluation
Claim: user - the refusal names the real problem
Before: walked: malformed body -> 400 'catalogId is required - a settle is scoped to one catalog'
After: predicted: 400 'settle body is not valid JSON'
Method: simulation - walked from the code; the S test was not built for round budget
Result: better
Gate: none
evidence: src/app/api/pipeline-artifacts/settle/route.ts:98 const body = (await req.json().catch(() => ({}))) as Record<string, unknown>;
instrument: route test: malformed body -> 400 whose error mentions JSON; empty and valid bodies unchanged
